slowdown.note: He said on the Senate floor that leading AI figures warn 'we're moving too fast' and asked whether Congress will listen, but he did not himself call for slowing AI development; his proposals are guardrails such as third-party evaluations.

pause.note: In his 29 September 2026 letter he described 'full stop' as one of 'the two extremes of the AI debate' and placed the real opportunity 'somewhere between full speed ahead and full stop'. This is an indirect rejection of a halt rather than an explicit statement against a pause; a reviewer may prefer 'none'.

intl.note: He did not sign the 23 September 2026 letter urging AI talks with China. His letter calls for stronger chip export restrictions and working with allies, which does not count.

rsi.note: No statement found on banning self-improving AI.

record: Sent a letter to President Trump (sole signer) urging federal AI guardrails: third-party evaluation of the most powerful models, accountability for knowingly deploying dangerous systems, incident reporting, and tighter chip export controls.
Called on the Senate Commerce Committee to hold hearings with AI industry leaders on regulation.
Reintroduced, with Sen. Capito, the VET AI Act directing the National Institute of Standards and Technology to write guidelines for independent third-party evaluations of AI systems.
Did not sign the 23 September 2026 letter from 17 senators urging AI talks with China (not on the verified signer list).
grade_reason: His 29 September 2026 letter to President Trump says AI systems are becoming 'more powerful and potentially uncontrollable' and warns of 'consequences both profound and irreversible'. The B rests on one short loss-of-control phrase and is a boundary with C; nothing found mentions extinction, superintelligence or bioweapons.
notes: Seven web searches ran, none refused. Opened and read in full: the 29 Sep 2026 and 17 Sep 2026 Senate press releases (raw page text; all quotes checked by exact string match against the page) and the 1 Aug 2025 VET AI Act release (through the page-fetch tool). Not opened: the CNBC Squawk Box interview of 29 Sep 2026 (https://www.cnbc.com/video/2026/09/29/sen-john-hickenlooper-presses-president-trump-on-ai-guardrails.html), the video (https://youtube.com/shorts/hPYqGXB8kKo) and the full 16 Sep floor speech; the floor quote is as excerpted by his office, with an ellipsis earlier in the excerpt, and its date is taken from the release's word 'Yesterday'. Quotes use the curly apostrophes shown on the page. Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act: search results name only Sanders (Senate) and Casar and other House Democrats; no source shows Hickenlooper as a co-sponsor, and the official co-sponsor list was not checked. Left out as not his own words: the release's summary that he criticized the administration for 'downplaying warnings from AI researchers'. The letter's cited incidents (an AI error nearly causing a naval confrontation with China; AI agents trying to escape a sandbox) are his descriptions and were not independently verified. The superintelligence, extinction, pause and China searches returned nothing by him. A 2017 NPR report on his reaction as governor to Elon Musk's AI warning predates the 2025 cut-off and was excluded.
